content.text: That was worse, so I'm going back to a width of 52 before exporting.

I built the part and exported it to `submission.step`. It's a single valid solid, and the STEP file reads back with the same volume and bounding box as the part.

**The part:** a flat plate 100 × 52 × 4 mm, lying in the XY plane with the thickness along Z. It has five parallel rectangular slots cut through it, running along X. Each slot is 62 × 3 mm, they're 9 mm apart in Y, and they're set toward the −X end. Alternate slots are shifted 6 mm along X from their neighbours, so the ends are staggered as in the reference.

**Match to the target:** the four-view silhouette comparison gave a mean IoU of **0.977** (0.976–0.978 per view). I tried a few width-to-length ratios:

| Plate (L × W) | Mean IoU |
|---|---|
| 100 × 60 | 0.867 |
| 100 × 66 | 0.800 |
| **100 × 52** | **0.977** |
| 100 × 54 | 0.947 |

I rolled back to the 52 mm version before exporting.

**Less certain:** the score only measures the outline, so it doesn't check the slots. Their width, length, spacing and stagger are estimated by eye from the reference image. The final grade is a voxel comparison against the real part, so how close the slots are will affect it slightly.

The part is built from a script, so it has no editable feature tree. That's fine for the STEP file, which is all that gets scored.

result:
I built the part and exported it to `submission.step`. It's a single valid solid, and the STEP file reads back with the same volume and bounding box as the part.

**The part:** a flat plate 100 × 52 × 4 mm, lying in the XY plane with the thickness along Z. It has five parallel rectangular slots cut through it, running along X. Each slot is 62 × 3 mm, they're 9 mm apart in Y, and they're set toward the −X end. Alternate slots are shifted 6 mm along X from their neighbours, so the ends are staggered as in the reference.

**Match to the target:** the four-view silhouette comparison gave a mean IoU of **0.977** (0.976–0.978 per view). I tried a few width-to-length ratios:

| Plate (L × W) | Mean IoU |
|---|---|
| 100 × 60 | 0.867 |
| 100 × 66 | 0.800 |
| **100 × 52** | **0.977** |
| 100 × 54 | 0.947 |

I rolled back to the 52 mm version before exporting.

**Less certain:** the score only measures the outline, so it doesn't check the slots. Their width, length, spacing and stagger are estimated by eye from the reference image. The final grade is a voxel comparison against the real part, so how close the slots are will affect it slightly.

The part is built from a script, so it has no editable feature tree. That's fine for the STEP file, which is all that gets scored.
